\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہچکچانا} (hichkichānā)}{ہچکچانا (hichkichānā)}]{\ur{ہچکچانا} (hichkichānā) — to hesitate}

\label{lesson:UR-C451-hichkichana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to whimper, then the Urdu for out of sight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہچکچانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ہچکچانا}} — \emph{hichkichānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to hesitate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{سوال} \ur{پوچھنے} \ur{سے} \ur{ہچکچاتی} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh savāl pūchhne se hichkichātī hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She hesitates to ask questions.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{ہچکچایا}, \emph{voh hichkichāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہچکچانا}} (\emph{hichkichānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi \emph{hicaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to draw back\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{hicc}, \textquotedblleft{}draw back\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 14083); the longer Urdu verb probably repeats it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hichkichānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hichkichānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh savāl pūchhne se hichkichātī hai.} — She hesitates to ask questions.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to whimper, then the Urdu for out of sight, then say \emph{hichkichānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ہچکچانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To hesitate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{لجانا} (lajānā)}{لجانا (lajānā)}]{\ur{لجانا} (lajānā) — to blush; to be bashful}

\label{lesson:UR-C451-lajana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for out of sight, then the Urdu for to hesitate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{لجانا}}
\textbf{\ur{لجانا}} — \emph{lajānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to blush; to be bashful\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دولہا} \ur{کو} \ur{دیکھ} \ur{کر} \ur{دلہن} \ur{لجا} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dūlhā ko dekh kar dulhan lajā gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bride blushed when she saw the bridegroom.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{لجا} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh lajā gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{لجانا}} (\emph{lajānā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{lajānā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be ashamed\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{lajjátē}, \textquotedblleft{}is ashamed\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10909).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lajānā}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ندامت} (nadāmat)}{ندامت (nadāmat)}]{\ur{ندامت} (nadāmat) — remorse}

\label{lesson:UR-C451-nadamat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to hesitate, then the Urdu for to blush.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ندامت}}
\textbf{\ur{ندامت}} — \emph{nadāmat} — \textquotedblleft{}remorse\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{جھوٹ} \ur{بول} \ur{کر} \ur{اسے} \ur{ندامت} \ur{ہوئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jhūṭ bol kar use nadāmat huī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After telling the lie he felt remorse.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ندامت}} (\emph{nadāmat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{nadāma}, \textquotedblleft{}regret\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پشیمان} (pashemān)}{پشیمان (pashemān)}]{\ur{پشیمان} (pashemān) — contrite; sorry (for what one did)}

\label{lesson:UR-C451-pasheman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to blush, then the Urdu for remorse.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پشیمان}}
\textbf{\ur{پشیمان}} — \emph{pashemān} — \textquotedblleft{}contrite; sorry (for what one did)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{اپنی} \ur{بات} \ur{پر} \ur{پشیمان} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh apnī bāt par pashemān thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He was sorry for what he had said.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پشیمان}} (\emph{pashemān}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{pashēmān}, \textquotedblleft{}regretful\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خجالت} (khijālat)}{خجالت (khijālat)}]{\ur{خجالت} (khijālat) — embarrassment}

\label{lesson:UR-C451-khijalat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for remorse, then the Urdu for contrite.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خجالت}}
\textbf{\ur{خجالت}} — \emph{khijālat} — \textquotedblleft{}embarrassment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{غلط} \ur{نام} \ur{لے} \ur{کر} \ur{مجھے} \ur{خجالت} \ur{ہوئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ghalat nām le kar mujhe khijālat huī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I was embarrassed at using the wrong name.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{خجالت}} (\emph{khijālat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{khajāla}, \textquotedblleft{}bashfulness, shame\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
